summary: Picks up where Section 0 Arrays leaves off — Kadane's algorithm for max subarray, point-update + range-query via difference arrays (Flip), the rain-water two-pointer trick, spiral matrix traversal, and search in row-and-column-sorted matrices. The pattern that keeps reappearing: pre-compute one auxiliary structure (max-so-far, suffix max, difference array) so a hard-looking nested loop collapses to O(N).

thoughtProcess.title: 1. Kadane: 'reset or extend'.
thoughtProcess.body: At every index ask: would adding A[i] to the running sum make things worse than starting fresh from A[i]? running = max(A[i], running + A[i]); best = max(best, running). One pass, O(N).

thoughtProcess.title: 2. Range updates + final read = difference array.
thoughtProcess.body: If the problem flips bits / adds K over many intervals and asks the final state, mark +1 at L and -1 at R+1 in an aux array. One prefix-sum pass at the end reconstructs the result in O(N + Q).

thoughtProcess.title: 3. Rain water: water above i = min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]) - A[i].
thoughtProcess.body: Precompute the two suffix/prefix maxes (or use the two-pointer trick to save space). Subtract A[i] and clamp to 0.

thoughtProcess.title: 4. Sorted matrix: stair-step search.
thoughtProcess.body: Start at top-right (or bottom-left). If current > target go left; if < target go down. O(R + C) — no binary search needed.

thoughtProcess.title: 5. Spiral / submatrix sums: layer + 2D prefix.
thoughtProcess.body: Spiral is just four bounded walks (top row, right col, bottom row, left col) in a shrinking rectangle. Submatrix sums use a 2D prefix table P[i][j] = sum of rect (0,0)→(i-1,j-1).

thoughtProcess.title: 6. 'Any-swap' problems only care about counts, not positions.
thoughtProcess.body: When you may swap any two elements (Minimum Swaps), the arrangement is fully controllable — the only real question is WHERE the K good elements must land. Recast as: over all length-K windows, how many bad elements sit inside? The minimum is the answer, because each bad element in the target block trades 1-for-1 with a good element outside.

thoughtProcess.title: 7. Monotone two pointers only work on positive arrays.
thoughtProcess.body: The sliding-window 'expand right / shrink left' for max sum <= B (Maximum Subarray Easy) relies on all C[i] > 0: adding only grows the sum, removing only shrinks it. The instant negatives are allowed this invariant breaks (shrinking can raise the sum) and you must fall back to prefix-sum / Kadane logic.

commonMistakes.title: Kadane initialised to 0 with all-negative input
commonMistakes.wrong:
int best = 0, run = 0;
for (int x : A) { run = Math.max(0, run + x); best = Math.max(best, run); }
commonMistakes.right:
int best = A[0], run = A[0];
for (int i = 1; i < N; i++) { run = Math.max(A[i], run + A[i]); best = Math.max(best, run); }
commonMistakes.why: Resetting run to 0 when all numbers are negative returns 0 instead of the least-negative element.

commonMistakes.title: Flip without difference array
commonMistakes.wrong: for each query (L, R): for (i = L; i <= R; i++) A[i] ^= 1;
commonMistakes.why: Per-query O(R - L) becomes O(N * Q). Difference array makes total work O(N + Q).

commonMistakes.title: Search in sorted matrix: full binary search per row
commonMistakes.why: Stair-step from top-right is O(R + C). Per-row BS is O(R log C). For square N×N the stair-step wins for any N > log N.

commonMistakes.title: Rain water clamp forgotten
commonMistakes.why: At the global max, min(left, right) equals A[i], so the contribution is 0 — but if you bracket wrong you get negative water.

commonMistakes.title: Spiral with one row / one column not handled
commonMistakes.why: Strict inequalities skip the last single-row / single-column band. Use <= and guard the bottom and left walks.

commonMistakes.title: Submatrix sum using 4 nested loops
commonMistakes.wrong: for r1 for c1 for r2 for c2 for i for j sum += A[i][j];
commonMistakes.right: // 2-D prefix P[i+1][j+1]; submatrix sum = P[r2+1][c2+1] - P[r1][c2+1] - P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1]
commonMistakes.why: Six nested loops is O(R^3 C^3). Prefix-table preprocessing is O(RC), each query O(1).

commonMistakes.title: Minimum Swaps: counting good-outside instead of bad-inside
commonMistakes.wrong: int good = countGood(window); ans = min(ans, K - good);
commonMistakes.right: if (A[r-K] > B) bad--; if (A[r] > B) bad++; ans = Math.min(ans, bad);
commonMistakes.why: Both equal (bad = K - good), but people forget the window is size K (not the whole suffix) and mix window lengths. Track bad-in-window directly; short-circuit K==0 / K==n to avoid an empty or full-window off-by-one.

commonMistakes.title: First Missing Positive: sign-marking without sanitising / abs
commonMistakes.wrong: for (int v : A) if (v <= N) A[v-1] *= -1;  // reads already-flipped values
commonMistakes.right:
// pass 1: v<=0 or v>N -> N+2 sentinel
// pass 2: val = Math.abs(A[i]); if (val <= N) A[val-1] = -Math.abs(A[val-1]);
commonMistakes.why: Once you start flipping signs, later A[i] may already be negative, so you must read Math.abs(A[i]) and negate via -Math.abs(...) so double-marking a repeat doesn't flip it back. Skipping the sentinel pass lets a stray 0 or huge value corrupt an index.

commonMistakes.title: Cyclic sort: using if instead of while, or wrong guard
commonMistakes.wrong: for (int i=0;i<N;i++) if (A[i]>0 && A[i]<=N) swap(i, A[i]-1); // one swap only
commonMistakes.right: while (A[i] > 0 && A[i] <= N && A[i] != A[A[i]-1]) swap(i, A[i]-1);
commonMistakes.why: A single if leaves swapped-in elements unplaced. The while keeps placing until index i is settled. The guard A[i] != A[A[i]-1] (compare VALUES) prevents an infinite loop on duplicates; total swaps stay <= N.

edgeCases: All-negative input for Kadane — return the largest (least-negative) single element.
Empty input or N=0 — early-return without dereferencing A[0].
Single-cell matrix — spiral / search / rain water must still work.
Range queries with L == R (single index).
Rain water at the global max — contribution is exactly 0, no crash.
Stair-step search target larger than every element — i walks past last row gracefully.
First missing positive when array is already 1..N — answer is N+1.
Merge intervals when input is empty or single interval — output is the same list.
Difference array index R+1 == N — allocate N+1, not N.
Spiral with R != C — bottom/left walks must be guarded by the if checks.
Minimum Swaps: K == 0 (no good elements) or K == n (all good) — return 0 without sliding.
Insert Interval: empty input set -> output is just [B]; B before/after all intervals — one while-phase copies nothing, the other copies everything.
Insert Interval: B touching two neighbours (e.g. [2,6] into [[1,3],[6,9]]) collapses BOTH into [1,9]; the widen-loop must keep consuming while A[i].start <= be.
Contribution / N^4-style product: cast to long BEFORE multiplying ((long)(i+1)*(N-i)*...); a 30x30 all-10s matrix already exceeds int.
Sorted-matrix staircase for lexicographically-smallest match: on equality keep moving LEFT (col--), prefer the lower row for duplicates — don't stop at the first hit.
